reason: E3 directly supports higher creep activation energy in HEAs vs. pure W and links it to lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion, but the cited evidence does not address homogeneous deformation, crack initiation, or toughness comparisons, leaving those premises unsupported.
premises: Severe lattice distortions in the HEA impede dislocation motion
Sluggish diffusion in the HEA increases creep activation energy
Increased creep activation energy promotes homogeneous plastic deformation
Homogeneous deformation delays crack initiation, enhancing toughness
Pure tungsten lacks these distortions, leading to localized strain and lower toughness
